name: AddWeb Cookies Popup
author: AddWeb Solution

sections.description:
AddWeb Cookies Popup shows a cookie notice to your visitors as a full-width belt (top or bottom) or a small box. It is lightweight: one small stylesheet and one small script, with no jQuery, and it works with page caching.

Choose the type of notice:

  • Information notice: a message with a Close button. It is shown again after the number of days you choose.
  • Consent banner: Accept and Reject buttons. The visitor’s choice is stored and passed on to Google tags (Google Consent Mode v2) and to plugins that support the WP Consent API.

Features

  • Full-width belt at the top or bottom, or a small box in the bottom-left corner.
  • Your own title, message (bold, italic and links), button texts and colours.
  • Link to your privacy policy page, taken automatically from Settings > Privacy.
  • Accept / Reject consent banner.
  • Google Consent Mode v2: Google Analytics, Ads and Tag Manager wait for consent.
  • WP Consent API support, so other plugins that support it can respect the choice.
  • “Cookie settings” link to let visitors change their choice: the [aws_cookie_settings] shortcode, or any link to #aws-cookie-settings.
  • Preview on site button for administrators.
  • Accessible: placed at the start of the page for keyboard and screen-reader users, real buttons, Escape to hide it, and focus returns to where the visitor was.
  • Translatable texts, and the notice texts can be translated per language with WPML or Polylang.
  • For developers: the awscp:consent JavaScript event, the awscp_get_consent() PHP function and the awscp_show_notice filter.

Important

This plugin shows the notice and records the visitor’s choice. It does not scan your site or block scripts added by other plugins or your theme. If your site needs prior consent for such scripts, make sure they respect Google Consent Mode or the WP Consent API, or load them only after consent.

External services

This plugin does not connect to any external service. When “Google Consent Mode v2” is turned on, it only adds a small inline script that sends consent signals to Google tags that are already on your site (added by your theme, Site Kit or another plugin); it does not load any Google script itself.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from Plugins > Add New, or upload the aws-cookies-popup folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Settings > Cookies Popup to change the text, the type of notice and the colours.
  4. Click Preview on site to see the result.
sections.faq:
Which cookies does the plugin set?

In information notice mode, aws_visited (value true) when the visitor closes the notice. In consent banner mode, aws_cookie_consent (value accepted or rejected). Both expire after the number of days set in the settings (15 by default).

How can visitors change their choice?

Add the [aws_cookie_settings] shortcode to a page or widget, or add a menu link pointing to #aws-cookie-settings. Clicking it opens the notice again.

Does it work with caching plugins?

Yes. The notice is part of every page and the script decides in the visitor’s browser whether to show it.

Can I translate the notice for a multilingual site?

Yes. The default texts are translatable, and with WPML or Polylang you can translate your own title, message and button texts per language (String Translation).

I updated from version 1. Do I need to change anything?

No. Your text, colours, position and cookie lifetime are kept, and visitors who already closed the notice will not see it again until their cookie expires. The message editor is now the WordPress editor instead of CKEditor.
sections.changelog:
2.0.0

  • New: Consent banner mode with Accept and Reject buttons.
  • New: Google Consent Mode v2 support.
  • New: WP Consent API support.
  • New: Privacy policy link (uses the page from Settings > Privacy, or your own address).
  • New: [aws_cookie_settings] shortcode and #aws-cookie-settings links let visitors change their choice.
  • New: “Preview on site” button.
  • New: WPML / Polylang support for the notice texts.
  • New: Developer event awscp:consent, function awscp_get_consent() and filter awscp_show_notice.
  • Improvement: The message is edited with the WordPress editor; the old CKEditor 4.5 from an external CDN is removed.
  • Improvement: New front-end script without jQuery (ready for jQuery 4 in WordPress 7.2); the bundled jQuery UI, jQuery Cookie and Font Awesome are removed.
  • Improvement: The close button is a real button, with keyboard support and screen-reader labels.
  • Improvement: Settings page rebuilt on the WordPress Settings API; only the fields that apply are shown.
  • Improvement: The notice works on mobile, sits below the admin bar for logged-in users and supports the “reduced motion” setting.
  • Fix: Every front-end page showed a critical error in version 1.5.2.
  • Fix: The notice was marked as seen as soon as it appeared, before the visitor closed it.
  • Fix: The button text colour setting had no default value.
  • Security: Only administrators can change the settings, every setting is validated, and all output is escaped.
  • Compatibility: Tested with WordPress 7.2; compatible with PHP 7.4 to 8.4. Requires WordPress 6.5 and PHP 7.4 or later.

  • Compatibility check with WordPress 6.3

  • UI fixes
